scope: TCP acceptance tools against loopback test fixtures
coverage: Three 1 MiB cycles through the actual checker and echo-service CLIs
Write half-close, exact response bytes and mandatory receive EOF
Corruption, truncation, extra bytes, early close and silent peer rejection
Complete response without EOF and late EOF rejection
Rate-limited echo and delayed client reads
Finite service lifetime, including an idle connected peer
Loopback default, explicit RFC1918 opt-in and invalid-input rejection
fixes: Use a high-resolution elapsed-time clock and guard zero-duration throughput.
Reject completion observed after the overall cycle deadline.

local_qa.disposition: Keep conclusions limited to the fixture set. Reviewer claims about partial TCP EOF and protocol framing do not apply to this transparent TCP echo checker. Fault-peer tests were independently inspected. Two broader source reviews exhausted model output without an answer.

limitations: No real SSH authentication or forwarding session.
No device identity, bulb memory, radio, throughput or recovery evidence.
Synthetic TCP success must not be reported as the hardware POC.
